# Hand-auditable analytics golden fixture

`golden-order-lines.csv` is a deliberately small canonical order-line dataset. `expected.json` is
hand-authored from the arithmetic below; it must not be generated by the analytics engine or by a
fixture helper.

All monetary calculations use integer cents. The dataset assumes USD and calendar dates in
`America/Chicago`.

## Cases represented

- `ORD-900001` has two product lines, but counts as one order. Its $3.00 marketing allocation appears
  only on `LINE-9000001`.
- `CUST-9001` has two orders, and `CUST-9002` has two orders. The other four customers have one order
  each.
- `LINE-9000005` has zero revenue because its $5.00 discount equals gross line value.
- `LINE-9000004`, `LINE-9000005`, and `LINE-9000007` have negative gross profit.
- `PROD-OUT-901` is negative in aggregate. `PROD-KIT-901` has one negative row but remains positive in
  aggregate.
- `CUST-9002` has intentionally missing `customer_segment` and `campaign` values on both orders. Its
  second order still has $2.00 marketing spend, proving that a missing campaign does not mean zero
  spend.
- February 29, March 1, March 31, April 1, April 30, and May 1 provide leap-day and month-boundary
  coverage.
- Products span Home, Kitchen, Outdoor, and Wellness; orders span all four regions and all three
  channels.

## Independent full-dataset calculations

There are nine lines, eight distinct orders, six distinct customers, and twelve units. Only
`ORD-900001` is multi-line.

```text
revenue = 1800 + 500 + 1000 + 800 + 0 + 900 + 1600 + 900 + 2000 = 9500 cents
cost    = 1200 + 200 + 600 + 1000 + 200 + 400 + 2000 + 600 + 500 = 6700 cents
profit  = 9500 - 6700 = 2800 cents
margin  = 2800 / 9500 = 28 / 95

discounts = 200 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 500 + 100 + 0 + 100 + 0 = 900 cents
spend     = 300 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 100 + 200 + 100 + 400 = 1100 cents
marketing contribution = 9500 - 6700 - 1100 = 1700 cents
marketing ROI = 1700 / 1100 = 17 / 11
average order value = 9500 / 8 cents; it must not be rounded before later calculations
```

The repeat-customer definition is at least two distinct order IDs. `CUST-9001` and `CUST-9002` are
repeat customers, so the full-dataset rate is `2 / 6`; the other four customers are one-time.

## Product reconciliation

| Product        |   Revenue |      Cost | Gross profit |       Orders | Quantity |    Customers |
| -------------- | --------: | --------: | -----------: | -----------: | -------: | -----------: |
| `PROD-HOM-901` |     3700c |     2400c |        1300c |            3 |        4 |            2 |
| `PROD-OUT-901` |     2400c |     3000c |        -600c |            2 |        3 |            1 |
| `PROD-WEL-901` |     2000c |      500c |        1500c |            1 |        1 |            1 |
| `PROD-KIT-901` |     1400c |      800c |         600c |            3 |        4 |            3 |
| **Total**      | **9500c** | **6700c** |    **2800c** | not additive |   **12** | not additive |

Product revenue ranks Home, Outdoor, Wellness, then Kitchen. Therefore:

```text
top-one share = 3700 / 9500 = 37 / 95
top-three share = (3700 + 2400 + 2000) / 9500 = 81 / 95
HHI = (3700^2 + 2400^2 + 2000^2 + 1400^2) / 9500^2 = 2541 / 9025
```

Top-five share is intentionally non-computable because the fixture has only four products.

Category revenue equals the corresponding product revenue. Region revenue is Central 2900c, East
2400c, South 0c, and West 4200c. Channel revenue is Marketplace 4400c, Retail Pop-up 0c, and Web
5100c. Each exhaustive partition sums to 9500c.

## Selected-period repeat semantics

March contains `ORD-900003`, `ORD-900004`, and `ORD-900005`: three lines, three orders, three
customers, four units, 1700c revenue, 1600c cost, 100c profit, 600c discounts, and 100c spend. Each
March customer has one order within March, so the in-selection repeat count is zero. `CUST-9002` is
nevertheless a repeat customer across the full loaded fixture because it orders again on April 1.
This distinction prevents the two repeat definitions from being conflated.
